title: Letter to Emma Smith, 26–27 June 1844
handwriting: Handwriting of Willard Richards and JS
source_note: JS, Letter, Carthage, Hancock Co., IL, to Emma Smith, Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, [26]–27 June 1844; handwriting of Willard Richards and JS; signatures of JS; two pages; CHL. Includes address, docket, and redactions. Two leaves measuring 9⅝ × 7⅝ inches (24 × 19 cm). The leaves were most likely conjugal leaves of a bifolium that are now separate. The leaves are ruled with twenty-seven printed lines, now faded. The letter was trifolded twice in letter style and addressed. The letter was refolded multiple times and there is separation along and tearing at the folds. The document has undergone conservation. The letter was retained by Emma Smith, who died in 1879, and passed down among Smith family descendants. It bears a docket in the handwriting of an unidentified scribe. Redactions on the manuscript correlate with changes to capitalization and punctuation made to the letter when it was published in The History of the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints in 1896, which indicates the letter had been transferred into the possession of the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints (now Community of Christ) by that time.1 In 2024, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints acquired the letter from the Community of Christ, and it is now held at the Church History Library in Salt Lake City.
